Aberdeen is the rural community around Bradner Road, south of Fraser Highway and north of the Abbotsford International Airport (YXX) lands.
Aberdeen is an official City name as well as a board name: it is profile area 6, Aberdeen, in the City's 2020 Demographic Profiles, separate from Bradner – Mt. Lehman and West Abbotsford.
Bradner Road runs north–south through the area, Fraser Highway forms the north edge, and Huntingdon Road and King Road run along the south toward YXX.
Bradner and Mt. Lehman lie to the west and northwest, Abbotsford West and Clearbrook to the east, and Poplar to the northeast.
There is no Aberdeen neighbourhood plan; Abbotsforward 2050 (Bylaw 2600-2016) governs.
Housing here is overwhelmingly single detached homes on rural and agricultural lots, not strata product.
Lot scale is agricultural: the minimum subdivision lot area is 8.0 hectares (ha) in the Agricultural One Zone (A1) and 16.0 ha in the Agricultural Two Zone (A2).
Homes are effectively all freehold farm and rural residential lots.
One townhome complex is confirmed at the western edge by the Aldergrove border: Lantern Park, 27640 Lantern Avenue, built by the Reimer Group.
That farm dwelling permission applies in accordance with the ALR Use Regulation, B.C. Reg. 30/2019, or as approved by the Agricultural Land Commission.

Land inside the Abbotsford Airport Zoning Regulations (AZR), SOR/83-253, shown on City drawing M-500, is subject to height limits, and NAV CANADA and Transport Canada approvals are required before the City issues a building permit.
Floodplain boundaries for any lot are set by Zoning Bylaw Schedule E and must be checked for that lot.

blocks.text: Aberdeen: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Aberdeen Elementary is the only public school confirmed inside the area, at 2975 Bradner Road.
Mt. Lehman Library at 5875 Mt. Lehman Road is to the northwest and Clearbrook Library at 32320 George Ferguson Way to the east.
Well records are held in the provincial GWELLS database, and onsite sewage filings are made through Fraser Health by an Authorized Person.
The nearest hospital is Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre at 32900 Marshall Road.

Lantern Park, 27640 Lantern Avenue, is the one completed townhome project confirmed at the area's western edge, built by the Reimer Group. Status (as of November 3, 2026): completed project named on a developer source.
The King and McKenzie Roads sports park proposal near Poplar is covered in the poplar note, not here.
The Aberdeen cost point is servicing: properties not connected to City water or sewer are not charged for those services, including lots using only well water or septic fields.
Route 21 (Aldergrove/Abbotsford) on Fraser Highway is the only bus route verified at the area's edge.
Huntingdon Road leads south toward the Huntingdon/Sumas border crossing corridor.
Abbotsford International Airport (YXX) lies south of the area.
Confirm ALR status and the lot's zone in the City WebMap before offering, because both are lot-specific.
Check whether the lot falls inside the AZR area on City drawing M-500 before planning any tall building.
Pull the well record in GWELLS and confirm the septic filing under the Sewerage System Regulation for any rural lot.
Check floodplain status against Zoning Bylaw Schedule E for the specific lot.

blocks.text: Along Bradner Road and Fraser Highway in west Abbotsford, Aberdeen is a rural community. It sits west of Clearbrook and northwest of Abbotsford International Airport.

faq.a: No, subdivision minimums are agricultural in scale. A1 lots subdivide at a minimum of 8.0 ha and A2 lots at 16.0 ha, so future subdivision value is limited by the zone rather than by frontage alone.
faq.q: Can a farm lot be subdivided into small lots?

faq.a: One Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit may be permitted on a qualifying lot. The A1 section requires a lot of at least 0.4 ha and caps the unit at 90 m² on lots of 40 ha or less, with ALR rules applying where the lot is in the reserve.
faq.q: Can a second home be added for family or workers?

faq.a: Yes, on land inside the AZR area on City drawing M-500. Height may not exceed the approach, outer or transitional surfaces, and federal approvals are needed before a City permit, which matters for tall shops and barns.
faq.q: Does the airport limit building height here?

faq.a: Aberdeen Elementary at 2975 Bradner Road is the public elementary school physically inside the sub-area, confirmed against the BC Ministry K-12 school file; the recorded SD34 School Locator run for that address returns Aberdeen Elementary as its elementary catchment, with Eugene Reimer Middle and Rick Hansen Secondary following it (SD34 School Locator, mybaragar.com, run 2026-11-01).
faq.q: Which elementary school is inside Aberdeen?

faq.a: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw 2400-2014 agricultural zones apply, with an A1 minimum subdivision lot area of 8.0 ha and A2 of 16.0 ha, plus Agricultural Land Reserve rules where the lot is in the ALR.
faq.q: What zoning controls a farm lot in Aberdeen?

faq.a: In the A1 zone, one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit is permitted per lot in accordance with the ALR Use Regulation, B.C. Reg. 30/2019, or as approved by the Agricultural Land Commission, on a lot of at least 0.4 ha, to a maximum of 90 m² on lots of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on lots over 40 ha; one secondary suite per lot, to 100 m², is also permitted in the City-hosted A1 section.
